## C&M table: one per analytics objective

| AO | Hypothesis | Key measures | Data source |
|:-----|:--------------------------|:--------------------------|:--------------|
| **AO1** Clover-online storefront | **H1:** Clover-to-online mismatches go with lower conversion and a smaller online revenue share | I.V.: availability and catalog mismatch, sync delay. D.V.: conversion rate, online revenue share | Clover and online store records |
| **AO2** Inventory and assortment | **H2:** Stronger historical demand goes with higher inventory turnover | I.V.: historical product demand. D.V.: inventory turnover | Clover sales and inventory reports |
| **AO3** SEO and paid search | **H3 (proposed):** Paid search visits convert at a higher rate than organic visits | I.V.: traffic source. D.V.: conversion rate. Also survey items on Google ads | GA4, Google Ads, survey items |
| **AO4** Digital loyalty program | **H4 (proposed):** Usefulness, ease of use, and trust each go with higher intention to use | I.V.: usefulness, ease of use, trust. D.V.: intention to use | **Customer survey** |

::: {.small}
Every table uses the same six columns: construct and definition, operationalization, source, type of scale, RQ/H, and role in analysis. **This questionnaire covers AO4.**
:::

## From H4 to the questionnaire

::: {.small}
**H4:** Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and trust in data handling are each positively associated with intention to use a digital loyalty program.
:::

| Construct | Role | Scale | Questions |
|:-------------------|:--------------|:----------------------------|:----------|
| Perceived usefulness | I.V. | Interval (multi-item, 5-point agreement) | Q13-Q16 |
| Perceived ease of use | I.V. | Interval (multi-item, 5-point agreement) | Q17-Q19 |
| Trust in data handling | I.V. | Interval (multi-item, 5-point agreement) | Q20-Q23 (Q22 reverse-coded) |
| **Intention to use** | **D.V.** | Interval (multi-item, 5-point agreement) | Q27-Q29 |
| Attitude toward the program | Exploratory | Interval (multi-item, 5-point agreement) | Q24-Q26 |
| Store usage, other loyalty programs, respondent type, age, gender | Control / grouping | Ordinal and nominal | Q2, Q4-Q8, Q12, Q33-Q34 |
| Eligibility | Screening | Nominal | Q1, Q3 |

::: notes
This is the traceability slide. Each hypothesis variable maps to a block of questions, and every other question has a role (control, grouping, screening, or descriptive).
:::

## The predictors: Section B items {.smaller}

| Q | Construct | Item (1 = Strongly disagree, 5 = Strongly agree) |
|:-----|:-------------|:----------------------------------------------------|
| Q13 | Usefulness | A digital loyalty program would be useful when I shop at the Farm Store. |
| Q14 | Usefulness | It would give me rewards or discounts I care about. |
| Q15 | Usefulness | It would make me feel my repeat purchases are recognized. |
| Q16 | Usefulness | A digital loyalty program would make it easier to keep track of my rewards. *(optional)* |
| Q17 | Ease of use | Signing up for a digital loyalty program would be easy. |
| Q18 | Ease of use | Using it at checkout would be simple and quick. |
| Q19 | Ease of use | I would not need help to learn how to use it. |
| Q20 | Trust | I would feel comfortable sharing my email or phone number to join. |
| Q21 | Trust | I trust the Farm Store to keep my personal information secure. |
| Q22 | Trust | I am concerned about how my purchase data would be used. *(reverse-coded)* |
| Q23 | Trust | I trust the Farm Store to use my purchase history only in ways I have agreed to. *(optional)* |

## The outcome: Section C items

| Q | Construct | Item (1 = Strongly disagree, 5 = Strongly agree) |
|:-----|:-------------|:----------------------------------------------------|
| Q24 | Attitude | I have a favorable attitude toward a digital loyalty program at the Farm Store. |
| Q25 | Attitude | A digital loyalty program is a good idea for the Farm Store. |
| Q26 | Attitude | I would rather use a digital loyalty program than a paper punch card. |
| Q27 | **Intention to use** | I would sign up for a digital loyalty program if it were offered. |
| Q28 | **Intention to use** | I would use it regularly when I shop at the Farm Store. |
| Q29 | **Intention to use** | I would recommend it to others. |

::: {.small}
Each multi-item scale will be checked with **Cronbach's alpha**. If the items hang together, we average them into one composite score. Q22 is reverse-coded first.
:::

## Screening, controls, and grouping

| Q | Question | Scale | Role |
|:-----|:----------------------------------|:-----------|:-------------|
| Q1, Q3 | Are you 18 or older? Purchased from the Farm Store in the past 12 months? | Nominal (Yes / No) | Screening |
| Q2 | Which best describes you? (student, faculty or staff, family or community, other) | Nominal | Grouping |
| Q4-Q6 | How often you buy, how recently, and typical spend per visit | Ordinal | Control |
| Q7 | Usual shopping channel (in person, online, both) | Nominal | Control |
| Q8-Q11 | Punch card use, plus satisfaction items if used | Nominal; Interval | Descriptive |
| Q12 | Number of other loyalty programs | Ordinal | Control |
| Q33-Q34 | Age range and gender | Ordinal; Nominal | Control |

::: {.small}
Category numbers (1, 2, 3...) on nominal questions are **labels only**.
:::

## Questionnaire flow and skip logic

| Section | Questions | Purpose | Logic |
|:----------------|:--------|:------------------------------|:------------------------|
| Cover page and consent | Consent | Study purpose, voluntary, anonymous, contact, 18+ confirmation | "No" = terminate survey |
| A. Screening and store usage | Q1-Q12 | Eligible customers; shopping behavior; punch card; other programs | Q1 or Q3 = No exits; Q9-Q11 only if Q8 = Yes |
| B. Perceptions | Q13-Q23 | Usefulness, ease of use, trust | |
| C. Attitude and intention | Q24-Q29 | Attitude, intention to use | |
| D. Preferences | Q30-Q32 | Joining method, rewards, consent to purchase records | |
| E. Demographics | Q33-Q34 | Age range, gender | |

::: {.small}
34 questions, about 8 to 10 minutes. Easy, relevant questions come first and personal questions come last.
:::
